name: Salmeterol
summary: Twice-daily long-acting beta-2 agonist for asthma only in combination with an ICS, and for COPD maintenance.
mechanism: Selective beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist that relaxes airway smooth muscle, with a bronchodilator effect lasting ~12 h.

dosing.adult: 50 mcg twice daily (DPI); 25 mcg, 2 puffs twice daily (MDI) — always with an ICS in asthma

safety.pregnancy: Inhaled — minimal systemic exposure; maintaining asthma control is the priority
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to salmeterol or lactose (DPI formulation)
warnings: LABA monotherapy in asthma increases the risk of asthma-related death — never use without an ICS
Not for relief of acute bronchospasm
Hypokalemia and hyperglycemia at high doses
safety.overdose: Beta-agonist excess: tremor, tachycardia, hypokalemia, arrhythmias — supportive care with ECG and potassium monitoring

indications: Prevention of exercise-induced bronchoconstriction (in patients already on ICS+LABA)
clinicalPearls: Slower onset than formoterol or salbutamol — it is not a rescue drug
The SMART trial linked salmeterol monotherapy to asthma deaths; ICS+LABA combination inhalers are the standard
good: 12-hour bronchodilation as the LABA half of ICS+LABA combination inhalers
bad: Monotherapy in asthma; acute symptom relief; exceeding the recommended dose
